name: Biscuit porcelain figures
summary: Unglazed white porcelain figures that look like marble and show the form with no colour. Vincennes and Sèvres made them after the paintings of Boucher and the models of Falconet, for the dessert table and the shelf.

philosophy.core_thesis: When the glaze and the colour are gone, only the form is left, so that a porcelain figure can look like fine marble in the hand.
design_principles: Leave the figure without glaze after the first firing, so that the surface stays matt and white.
Fire a soft-paste body to about 1100 °C, so that the grain is fine and the edge is soft.
Model the figure after a painter or a sculptor: a pastoral group, a child, a classical goddess.
Cast the figure from piece moulds, and finish each seam with a knife and a damp brush.
Keep the surface smooth, with a fine grain like sugar, and a slight warm cream tone.
Make the figure 15 to 40 cm high, on a plain base with a small moulded edge.
Use no enamel. Allow a single touch of gilt or a coloured glaze on the base only.
Show the folds, the hair and the ribbons in sharp, shallow relief that catches light.
anti_patterns: A glossy glaze over the whole figure
A bright enamel painting on the face and the dress
A heavy earthenware body with a coarse grain
A rough, uneven surface with visible mould seams
A sharp, cold white with a blue tint
A pose full of lace and small flowers that hides the form

form.shape: Pastoral and mythological figures: children, nymphs, bathers, shepherd groups and small busts, in a calm classical pose.
form.profile: A smooth, rounded outline with soft flesh and clear folds; the pose is natural and turns only a little.
form.foot_and_rim: A plain round or oval base with a small moulded edge, often on a rock or a tree trunk that gives support to the figure.
form.proportion: Height 15 to 40 cm; the wall is 3 to 5 mm thick, and the proportion is natural, after a child or a young adult.
rules: Leave all of the surface without glaze.
Keep the grain fine and the surface smooth.
Use a rock, a tree stump or a column as a support.
Take the pose from a known painting or a sculpture.
Show flesh by smooth, soft planes and cloth by sharp, shallow folds.

bodies.rule: Use a fine, white, dense paste that fires to a matt, sugar-like surface. After 1769 a hard paste also serves; keep the colour a pale warm white.

methods: modelling of a master figure by a sculptor
joining and fettling of seams by hand
forming.joins: The parts are cast apart and joined with slip. The seams are cut and sponged until they disappear, so the surface is one smooth plane.
forming.details: A fine matt grain, a small vent hole in the base, and a sharp edge to the folds that no glaze rounds.

glaze.pattern: No colour. The only pattern is the relief of the form: folds, hair, ribbons, leaves and a few incised lines.
glaze.gloss: Matt, 0 to 5 GU, with a soft sheen like marble.
glaze.wear: The surface takes dust and stains, and it marks easily with oil from the hand. Chips show a white, sugary body.

palette.strategy: One warm white and its shadow tones, so that the light on the form is the only colour.

firing.kiln: A wood-fired kiln with saggars at Vincennes, later a larger kiln at Sèvres.
processes: single firing without glaze at about 1100 to 1250 °C
optional touch of gilt on the base
firing.scale: A royal manufactory with sculptors, moulders and repairers; hundreds of figures a year after 1757.
firing.signs: A matt surface with no gloss, a fine vent hole, a sharp edge to the folds and a mark under the base.

pieces.form: Pastoral group of a shepherd and a shepherdess after a painting by Boucher
Child with a bird, seated on a rock, with soft flesh
Bust of a king on a plinth, with a laurel and a ribbon
Bather who steps out of the water, with a drape
Classical group of a goddess with a cupid, on a column

positive: soft flesh and sharp shallow folds
child with a bird on a rock

evidence.title: Vincennes biscuit pair, Dancer and Bagpiper
Sevres biscuit Pygmalion and Galatea, after Falconet

emotion.target_response: A quiet, tactile calm: the viewer wants to touch a white form that holds light like marble and shows a gentle scene with no colour.

use_cases: a museum label for a biscuit figure
a prompt for a matt white porcelain figure
a collector's brief for French porcelain
avoid_when: the brief wants a coloured and glazed figure
the brief wants a cheap earthenware figure
the brief needs a large heroic sculpture

modifiers.how: Add a clear glaze, paint overglaze enamels and gilding, and twist the pose into an S-curve.
Change to a parian body, scale up to 30 to 60 cm, and use a classical or sentimental subject with a smooth, cast surface.
